log.reply:
# Tamarack Instruments: Executive Briefing Proposal

Dear Dana Whitfield,

## Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has deployed a customer service chatbot on its support portal, is piloting AI visual inspection on the German production line and plans AI sales forecasting next year. Your stated objective is to have governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027. An internal audit finding of June 2026 recorded no inventory of AI systems. ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, although the start date is not fixed.

## What the Briefing Covers for Tamarack Instruments

The Briefing maps the EU AI Act and GDPR to each use case as expectations to verify with counsel, not as legal advice. For the chatbot, this includes likely transparency expectations toward users and the constraint that customer data must stay in the EU. For visual inspection, it addresses how the system may be classified and how consulting the German works council before anything touches production staff affects sequencing. United States requirements appear only as a general landscape item because the Profile lists no US driver.

We then assess readiness at a Piloting maturity level, starting with the missing AI inventory. We outline an operating model using the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen), with board oversight drawn from AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). We also consider where AI governance could connect to the ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 frameworks listed for the Client, without assuming any existing register or control. Three principles guide the session: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. The Briefing prepares the ground for ISO/IEC 42001 work but does not promise certification or audit outcomes.

## Logistics and Price

The Executive Briefing is a two-hour live virtual session priced at US$3,000, which is within the US$80,000 budget approved for this fiscal year. It is designed for the listed audience roles: General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. The session date is Unknown.

## What You Receive Afterward

After the session, the Client receives a summary memo. It records the decisions surfaced and our readiness observations. It also sets out three prioritized recommendations, each mapped to a next program option with its price, duration and a proposed timeline.

## Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. Please confirm a preferred session date and the attendee list.

Kind regards,

Senior AI Governance Consultant
AI Governance Academy

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: 'For visual inspection... how consulting the German works council before anything touches production staff affects sequencing' applies a stated constraint to a stated system. I treated it as a consequence of the constraint and not as a new fact, in line with the v1.14.3 guidance. Another scorer could read it as implying a works council relation.

'It is designed for the listed audience roles' restates the AUDIENCE_ROLES field and does not say who attends. I treated it as not asserting an unstated relation. A strict scorer could object, but the wording stays at the field level.

'which is within the US$80,000 budget approved for this fiscal year' is an arithmetic comparison of two stated figures. It does not claim the Briefing will be paid from that budget, so I did not count it as an inferred relation.

'likely transparency expectations toward users' and 'how the system may be classified' are general regulatory expectations framed conditionally and as items to verify with counsel. I did not treat them as Client facts.

The word count of about 430 depends on counting URLs as one word each and including the title heading. Even if each URL counted as several words, the total would plausibly stay near or under 450, but a different counting convention could shift it.
score.reasoning: All seven checklist items are met and no fail indicator appears. Every Client-specific statement traces to a Profile Block field. The letter introduces no incumbent register, process, control or owner beyond the listed framework names, and it hedges explicitly on ISO 27001 and ISO 9001. The decision date is phrased as the block states it. Program name, duration and price are unaltered. At about 430 words, the letter is within the 450-word limit and uses prose only. The closing line is present.
